**Status: detailed implementation plan; targets are not wired.** This page
plans [`5_clean_sect2022_construct_healthsheds.R`][legacy-5] and the spatial
helpers from [`999_utility_functions.R`][legacy-999]. Its outputs are the
cleaned 2022 FKT-to-clinic assignments and clinic healthshed geometries.

Spatial objects remain ordinary `sf` targets, serialized by targets. Persisted
nonspatial tables and evidence use Parquet file targets. The plan does not
introduce a new spatial interchange format or require repeated shapefile
round trips between stages.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Inventory Geometry And Reviewed Matching Evidence"}

Require `s1_gesis_xwalk_clean_df` from [page 19](19_page-clean-mapping-dhis2-gesis.qmd),
the staged input inventory, the 2022 sectorization, the 2018 sectorization,
the OCHA/BNGRC administrative polygons and code lookup, and every reviewed
match/unmatch/correction file used by the source.

Track the complete shapefile dataset, including companion files, or its
containing source archive. Preserve raw source formats and review notes.
Record source CRS, geometry validity, lookup-sheet number, identifier types,
and the local source revision before implementing matching.

Keep three decisions explicit: allowed shared FKT assignments, population
counting, and accepted residual non-contiguity. Historical coverage counts
do not prove those policies. Record the `sf`, GEOS/GDAL/PROJ, and topology
settings used for the reference comparison before changing the environment.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Declare The Spatial Helpers Beside Their First Use"}

Declare tracked function targets for the grouped string-distance join and
healthshed aggregation. Keep the cardinal-direction lookup with the matching
evidence if the migrated transformation needs it. Reuse page 18's CSV-reader
responsibility; do not create a second sparse-measurement reader here.

| Helper contract | Behavior to preserve |
| --- | --- |
| Grouped fuzzy join | Administrative grouping, cosine distance, case handling, candidate-selection callback, ties, unmatched groups, and optional unnesting |
| Clinic aggregation | Union of assigned geometry, population from distinct `(fkt_uid, fkt_pop_2022)` pairs, administrative attributes, FKT counts, connected components, and polygon parts |
| Empty geometry | Explicit construction with the input CRS inside the helper; no dependency on an untracked `empty_geom` global |

Replace the unresolved `source("scripts/0_utility_functions.R")` reference with
these explicit dependencies on the reviewed `999` implementation. Do not
rename the source file locally merely to make the old `source()` succeed.
Specify additional spatial package dependencies when these helpers are
implemented, then resolve the project lockfile through the existing workflow.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Repair Source Geometry And Split Nosy Mitsio"}

Build `s5_fkt_shapes_initial_sf` from the tracked polygons with the source's
validity repair. Reproduce the split of `MG71717150005` and its corresponding
`717150005` sectorization/lookup identifiers, including the reviewed suffixes.
Create `s5_fkt_code_lookup_initial_df` from lookup sheet 5 with character codes.

Capture the identity of the island and mainland pieces before relying on
polygon-part ordering. The legacy first-part versus later-part grouping is
order-sensitive; a changed library's part order must not silently swap the
assignments. Test area/coverage conservation and lookup consistency without
assuming that a topology repair is numerically identical across versions.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Reconcile Duplicate FKT Codes And Population"}

Normalize the sectorization schema in `s5_sectorization_2022_source_df` and read
the reviewed duplicate decisions separately in
`s5_sectorization_duplicate_reviews_df`. Build
`s5_sectorization_population_reconciled_df` with the original note-driven
precedence: retain approved shared assignments, delete the designated zero-
population record, and combine the populations for reviewed keep/delete pairs.

Retain review provenance and explain every row-count change. The historical
21927-to-21921 change and unchanged population total are reference observations.
Do not apply a generic `distinct(fkt_uid)` that would erase shared assignments
or change the source's population rule.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Apply Initial Matching Rounds In Their Reviewed Order"}

| Proposed target | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `s5_sectorization_fkt_match_reviews_list` | Ordered reviewed matching tables and their provenance |
| `s5_sectorization_fkt_matches_df` | Valid original codes followed by the reviewed fills, with `match_type` |
| `s5_sectorization_direct_matches_df` | Reviewed clinic assignments not represented by an existing FKT row |
| `s5_sectorization_initial_geometry_sf` | Lookup PCODE and attached FKT geometry |

Keep each correction round's precedence visible in a short procedure and
target declaration when implementation begins. Preserve leading zeros and
reviewed manual overrides. Record conflicting or multiply matched codes
instead of resolving them through incidental input order.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Evaluate Topology Before Removing Isolated Matches"}

Create `s5_sectorization_initial_topology_sf` with adjacency, component, and
isolation evidence. Reproduce the legacy DE-9IM relation test; do not replace
it with a different spatial predicate without a parity test. Point contacts,
line contacts, overlapping pieces, and holes need separate fixtures.

Apply the reviewed unlinking rule to
`s5_sectorization_contiguity_filtered_sf`, protecting the manual assignments
the source exempts. Build `s5_healthshed_clinic_initial_sf` with the same
aggregation helper used for every later version. Keep component count and
polygon-part count as distinct diagnostics.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Recover Historical Matches And Apply Follow-Up Reviews"}

Build the 2018 source table, join it through the cleaned GESIS mapping, and
retain the candidate's clinic, adjacency, and existing-healthshed evidence.
The proposed stages are `s5_sectorization_2018_candidates_sf`,
`s5_sectorization_2018_matches_sf`, and
`s5_sectorization_historical_filled_sf`.

Preserve grouped name matching and the historical distance cutoff `<= 0.11`.
Minimum-distance ties remain visible. Apply the subsequent manual matches,
unmatches, and geometry refreshes in `s5_sectorization_reviewed_v2_sf`, then
rebuild `s5_healthshed_clinic_v2_sf`. Do not let a later fuzzy candidate
overwrite an earlier reviewed decision without the source's explicit rule.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Evaluate Commune Candidates With The Contiguity Guard"}

Create `s5_sectorization_commune_candidates_sf` by matching within district,
retaining the closest commune with one clinic and distance `< 0.075`.
Evaluate the proposed additions in `s5_sectorization_commune_topology_sf`
before applying them. Preserve the guard against worsening component counts.

Apply accepted candidates to `s5_sectorization_commune_filled_sf` and rebuild
`s5_healthshed_clinic_v3_sf`. Keep rejected candidates and their reasons as
small diagnostic targets or Parquet evidence; the check block will inspect
those results rather than regenerate matching decisions.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Apply Final Reassignments And Island Corrections"}

Apply the reviewed non-contiguous reassignments, unmatched-FKT fixes,
duplicate/administrative corrections, coastal-island splits, and final
unlink/replacement rows in source order. The assignment chain ends in
`s5_sectorization_2022_clean_sf`; the final aggregation is
`s5_healthshed_clinic_final_sf`.

Retain named intermediate targets for the reassigned, unmatched-fixed,
miscellaneous-fixed, island-fixed, and final-unlinked states listed in the
[mapping inventory](mapping/legacy-pipeline-map.qmd#script-5-sectorization-and-healthsheds).
Each island split must update geometry and the code lookup together, with
population treatment recorded. Rebuild healthsheds from the corrected
assignment table rather than patching the unioned geometry independently.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Expose Spatial Handoffs And Review Evidence"}

Pages [24](24_page-locate-clinics.qmd) and [25](25_page-combine-clinic-metadata.qmd)
will consume the two final `sf` targets directly. This avoids shapefile field
name truncation and an extra RDS/shapefile export chain. Optional nonspatial
assignment or diagnostic exports must be Parquet file targets under
`data/intermediates/`.

Keep per-clinic non-contiguous and multipart review maps as ordinary plot-list
targets. Do not render protected maps or exception tables into the public
manual. Small diagrams or synthetic geometries can explain the checks.
Track any approved publication export under the separate release contract.

Parallelize only independent candidate batches or per-clinic diagnostics
after their shared input state is fixed. Correction rounds remain ordered;
running versions v1–v4 simultaneously would violate their dependencies.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Specify Spatial Acceptance Evidence"}

Implement `tests/check-healthshed-rules.R` using synthetic geometry before
wiring these targets. The future checks must establish:

| Check | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Geometry identity | CRS, valid geometry, correct island/mainland assignment, complete code-lookup updates, and conserved source coverage within a declared tolerance |
| Population | Repeated identical UID/population pairs count once; reviewed population merges conserve totals; shared clinic assignments remain intentional |
| Matching | Group boundaries, missing strings, distance thresholds, ties, and the precedence of reviewed overrides |
| Topology | Empty geometries, point/line contacts, disconnected pieces, holes, protected manual assignments, and the commune contiguity guard |
| Final coverage | Unmatched FKT, clinics without assigned FKT, residual component counts, and multipart geometry counts reported separately |
| Reproducibility | Same accepted assignments and population summaries on repeated runs, with package/geometry-engine provenance |

Compare legacy observations such as 2773 healthsheds and 26 multi-component
healthsheds against the exact input revision; do not turn them into universal
invariants or assert that healthsheds must be disjoint. Validate final source
membership and reviewed overlap exceptions independently of total counts.

No spatial targets or data-level checks have run as part of this plan.

```sh
python3 tests/check-manual-structure.py
```
